html:
The Panglong Agreement was signed on 12 February 1947 by Aung San and leaders of the Shan, Kachin and Chin peoples, who agreed to join a union with Burma proper in return for autonomy.

It made possible the independence of the Union of Burma on 4 January 1948. Aung San, however, was murdered in July 1947, and the Karen and others were not party to the deal.

The promise of self-rule was never kept. Ethnic revolts began soon after independence, starting with the Karen conflict, and grew after Ne Win's coup. 12 February is still Union Day, and ethnic groups still cite Panglong. See Shan States.
sum: The Panglong Agreement was signed on 12 February 1947 by Aung San and leaders of the Shan, Kachin and Chin peoples, who agreed to join a union with Burma proper in return for autonomy.
